name: Hassenuah
overview: Hassenuah is a male figure from the tribe of Benjamin, noted primarily as the father of Judah according to Nehemiah 11:9. There are no additional notes or detailed background information provided about him. His mention is brief but establishes a genealogical link within the tribe of Benjamin.
namesAndTitles: The name Hassenuah means "the hated one." This proper name is not indicated as being given by God, and it appears specifically in Nehemiah 11:9. The meaning of his name may reflect a particular character or circumstance, though the biblical text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Hassenuah as the father of Judah, an inferred relationship from Nehemiah 11:9. He is also explicitly identified as a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hassenuah's significance lies in his role as a genealogical link within the tribe of Benjamin. By being the father of Judah, he connects to the broader narrative of Israel's tribal lineage. His mention in Nehemiah 11:9 situates him within the post-exilic community, highlighting the preservation of tribal identities and family lines important to biblical history and God's covenant people.
